body:
IMHO, I think it would be better if we could limit the scope at the C# side so that no newer API is added to the core. At the end of the day, GDScript doesn't need such APIs, and in C#, communicating through the binding layer isn't performant enough.


I'm proposing an alternative approach, as the wrapper object (Godot.Collection.Dictionary) is the allocation concern, is there a way we can modify the [bindings generator](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp) to make it recongnize certain methods, and generate alternative, non-allocating api that marshals the native [godot_dictionary](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/InteropStructs.cs#L848) directly to a struct?

Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think with your proposal there still would be extraneous allocations made (the `IntersectRayResult` object will be allocated on the heap)? In case of doing a raycast every frame at 144fps: `64 bytes * 144 fps ~= 9KB` every second.

I think if `IntersectRayResult` was a `readonly ref struct` then it would be on the stack.

@adamwych 

> here still would be extraneous allocations made (the IntersectRayResult object will be allocated on the heap)?

What you said is true for `record`, but here I'm using `record struct`, which is effectively a `struct` with syntactic sugar.

> I think if `IntersectRayResult` was a readonly `ref struct` then it would be on the stack.

The `struct` defaults to being allocated on the stack, while the `ref struct` only prohibits the developer from putting it on the heap (that is, banning the developer from storing the struct as a member of the reference type). 

Is the `ref struct` approach really necessary? The need to store results on the heap for other NonAlloc method variations does exist, and I don't see a solid reason to prohibit the developer from doing so.


* Of course, `VariantUtils.ConvertToGodotObject(colliderValue)` might allocate a new wrapper once for the `collider` target if it never enters the C# land, but not for further calls with the same result target.

Okay, I misread that as a regular `record`.

Then I guess the proposal is good, certainly better than writing all those no alloc funcs by hand, but FYI I'm afraid this big of a change is outside of my scope of expertise and interest as I would rather continue working on my game right now, and it sounds like I would need to spend significant time figuring out how the bindings generator works.

@adamwych 

>  and it sounds like I would need to spend significant time figuring out how the bindings generator works.

Yes, I'm waiting to implement this feature when the struct in Godot is officially supported (effectively marshalls the native Godot struct directly to C# struct).

>  it sounds like I would need to spend significant time figuring out how the bindings generator works.

If all you need is just this API for your development, I think you can start your own fork based on the latest release. All you need to do is add a new partial class (see how we are adding additional methods to types in [Compat.cs](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Compat.cs)) and copy-paste my code (before you compile C# bindings).

```cs
public record struct IntersectRayResult(
    Vector3 Position,
    Vector3 Normal,
    long FaceIndex,
    long ColliderId,
    GodotObject Collider,
    long Shape,
    Rid Rid
)
```

Currently, it is impossible to automatically generate such a structure. This method only returns a dictionary, without any type information.

The approach of this PR writes the result into a RefCounted, which is also no alloc  for GDScript.

So there are two approaches for C#: write the no alloc API by hand, or improve the API of Godot itself. (The latter may have better performance, which completely avoids Dictionary allocation.)

@beicause 

> Currently, it is impossible to automatically generate such a structure. This method only returns a dictionary, without any type information.

That's correct. I specifically mentioned that I am waiting for [struct](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/QTu9nG79BRxe8YyqD) support in Godot because it is essential for properly handling APIs that return or accept C# structs. Hardcoding conversions into the binding generator is unlikely to be a desirable solution for anyone.

> The approach of this PR writes the result into a RefCounted, which is also no alloc for GDScript.

Given that the struct support is on the way, I don't think the team would accept this workaround.
Is this still relevant after the aforementioned merged PR?
No, I believe this PR is superseded by #113970 so I'm closing this one.
